lesson.text: Quick memory: last unit, percent. What is 50% of 30? Half of 30: 15.
A conversion is a ratio: 1 hour to 60 minutes is 1 : 60. Use it like any equal ratios: 2 : 120, 3 : 180.
To change a big unit to a small one, multiply: 3 hours = 3 × 60 = 180 minutes.
To change a small unit to a big one, divide: 150 minutes = 150 ÷ 60 = 2.5 hours.
Common ratios: 1 day = 24 hours, 1 week = 7 days, 1 year = 12 months, 1 m = 100 cm, 1 kg = 1,000 g.
Try it in the world: a game day is a set number of real minutes. Time one sunrise to the next, then work out how many game days fit in one real hour. Next: dividing fractions.

exercises.explain: 2 days = 48 hours; the others are 40 and 36.

exercises.prompt: A film is 135 minutes long. How many hours is that?
exercises.explain: Minutes to hours is small to big, so divide: 135 ÷ 60 = 2.25 hours. A quarter of an hour is 15 minutes, so it is 2 hours and 15 minutes.

exercises.prompt: A puppy is 30 months old. How old is it in years?
exercises.explain: Months to years is small to big, so divide by 12: 30 ÷ 12 = 2.5 years, which is 2 years and 6 months.

exercises.prompt: Match each amount to the same amount in the other unit.
exercises.explain: 2 hours = 120 minutes; 3 weeks = 21 days; 1.5 kg = 1,500 g; 48 hours = 2 days.

exercises.prompt: Sort the conversions: multiply or divide?
exercises.hint: Big unit to small: multiply. Small unit to big: divide.
exercises.explain: Hours to minutes, kg to g and days to hours go big to small: multiply. Minutes to hours and months to years go small to big: divide.

exercises.prompt: A game day lasts 20 real minutes. How many game days pass in 5 real hours?
exercises.hint: Change the hours into minutes first, then see how many 20s fit.
exercises.explain: 5 hours is 5 × 60 = 300 minutes. Each game day is 20 minutes: 300 ÷ 20 = 15 game days.
